newsitem.title: USA: Sprint Spectrum says no new PageNet deal.
newsitem.headline: Sprint Spectrum says no new PageNet deal.

text.p: Sprint Spectrum on Tuesday denied press and analysts' reports that it was about to launch a bundled service of Paging Network Inc (PageNet) pagers with its Personal Communications Services (PCS) wireless phones.

Sprint already offers Pagenet paging to its long distance service customers, and said it does eventually expect to resell pagers side by side with PCS phones -- already allowed for in a deal tied up with PageNet in December.
"Nothing has changed in our relationship with PageNet," said Sprint Spectrum spokesman Ed Mattix.
The news is a disappointment for paging, which has endured a crisis of credibility in recent months, analysts say.
PageNet stock was 1/2 lower at 18-1/2 in morning trade on Tuesday, having risen a similar amount on Monday.
Leading paging stocks like Mobile Telecommunications Technologies Corp, Arch Communications, Metrocall Inc and PageMart Wireless are all trading at a fraction of their 12-month highs.
Some investors have bailed out, bruised by management upheavals, delays in new products, and broken banking covenants in some previous high-fliers.
On top of this has been the fear that pagers will be replaced by PCS phones, which carry pagers in them but do not use the frequencies and licenses of existing paging companies.
However, paging analysts believe pagers built into PCS phones will be more limited in battery life, have less building penetration and a more limited geographic coverage than existing pagers.
"Net net, PCS does need paging," said analyst Christopher Larsen of Natwest Securities.
Sprint Spectrum, noting that in-built pagers would probably not be available in many of its areas at first, declined to take sides in the paging industry debate.
Sprint Spectrum is owned by Sprint Corp , and cable TV firms Comcast Corp Cox Communications Inc and Tele-Communications Inc.

"We have never said PCS phones are a replacement for pagers," Mattix said. He predicted that some customers would find separate pagers more convenient than in-built PCS pagers, and expected the company would market whatever was required.
"We have said all along we intend to offer pagers with many other services," he said.

American Personal Communications (APC), a Sprint Spectrum affiliate which has the only working PCS service in the U.S., said it has no plans to market PageNet pagers in its Washington D.C.-Baltimore licence area.
However, there are reasons to believe pagers could happily co-exist with PCS phones as a bundled product.
Natwest's Larsen said it would make sense to sell pagers at almost no cost to PCS phone users because each beep could generate a PCS call.
"A couple of calls generated per month on the PCS phone will pay for the pager," he said. -- New York Newsroom 212 859 1712
